qa_pairs.question: When starting CFX from an OnDemand desktop, what command-line arguments should be used for graphics, depending on whether a GPU was requested?
qa_pairs.answer: When starting CFX from an OnDemand desktop, use `cfx5 -graphics mesa` if you did not request a GPU when the desktop was started. If you did request a GPU, use `cfx5 -graphics ogl`.

qa_pairs.question: How do users launch the Mechanical APDL (Mapdl) GUI from the command line on an OnDemand desktop?
qa_pairs.answer: To launch the Mechanical APDL (Mapdl) GUI from the command line on an OnDemand desktop, first load the necessary module (e.g., `module load StdEnv/2023 ansys/2022R2`). Then, you can either type `mapdl -g` or type `launcher` and click the `RUN` button. These steps work whether your desktop session uses a GPU or not.

qa_pairs.question: How does one start Ansys Workbench on an OnDemand desktop when accelerated graphics are not required, and what is the graphical implication?
qa_pairs.answer: To start Ansys Workbench on an OnDemand desktop when accelerated graphics are not required, specify 'GPU Node' to select a compute node without a GPU for your OnDemand session. In a terminal, load the module (e.g., `module load StdEnv/2023 ansys/2025R2.04`) and then run `runwb2`. This configuration uses Mesa software emulation for OpenGL calls, avoiding the use of a more expensive GPU node.
